title: Protocol for high-throughput cloning, expression, purification, and evaluation of bispecific antibodies
protocol: Resuspend synthesized DNA fragments in deionized water to a final concentration of 5 ng/μL.
Dilute vector in deionized water to a final concentration of 5 ng/μL.
Set up Golden Gate Reactions in 96-well PCR plates.
Prepare enough master mix for 1.2× number of samples.
Seal the PCR plates with a thermal plate sealer.
Mix thoroughly and quickly spin plates at 500 g for 1 min.
Set up the Golden Gate thermocycler reaction.
Remove pre-dispensed chemically competent bacterial cells from −80°C storage and thaw on ice for 5 min.
Add 1.5 μL of Golden Gate Reaction to each well of competent cells using a multichannel pipet.
Gently mix by tapping the wall of the tube.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Heat shock cells at 42°C for 1 min using a pre-warmed thermocycler with a heated lid set to 104°C.
Place on ice for 1 min after heat shock.
Add 80 μL recovery medium to cells.
Seal plate and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Plate cells onto standard LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin using sterile glass beads or another preferred method.
Incubate the agar plates at 37°C overnight.
Prepare growth medium (LB broth + 100 μg/mL carbenicillin).
Use a multichannel pipette to aliquot growth medium into 96-well deep well blocks (1 mL per well).
Inoculate each well with a single colony from a successful transformation.
Grow bacterial culture overnight at 37°C in an incubator with shaking set to 1,200 RPM.
Purify transfection-grade DNA (∼30–50 μg per sample) using the QIAGEN Plasmid plus 96 Kit following manufacturer’s recommendations.
Measure concentration of purified DNA by assessing absorbance at 260 nm (A260).
Dilute DNA samples to a final concentration of 50-200 ng/μL with deionized water.
Prepare 96-well sequencing plates by adding 10 μL of diluted DNA sample per well using a multichannel pipette or VIAFLO 96 channel electronic pipette.
Verify construct identity through Sanger sequencing using vector forward primer: 5′-ACGAGGAGGATTTGATATTCACC-3′ and vector reverse primer: 5′-CTTCCGAGTGAGAGACAC-3′.
Analyze Sanger sequencing results using Geneious software.
Pool sequencing-confirmed DNA using an automatic liquid handler according to manufacturer instructions.
Mix plasmid DNA encoding each chain of a bispecific antibody at defined ratios (i.e., HC1:LC1:HC2:LC2 = 1:1:1:1).
Normalize concentration of the mixed DNA to 100 ng/μL.
Validate the concentration of each sample by measuring A260 of the mixed DNA using DropSense96 or similar instrument.
Store mixed DNA at 2°C–8°C for several weeks, or at −20°C for long-term storage.
Seed cells into a shake flask at a density of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL twenty-six hours before transfection.
Measure the viable cell density (VCD) and cell viability using the Vi-CELL XR viability analyzer on the day of transfection.
Warm culture medium and DNA to 20°C–25˚C.
Ensure that the cell density is between 1.8 to 2.2 × 10^6 cells/mL at the time of transfection, with >98% viability.
Gently aliquot cells into 96-well deep-well blocks (0.45 mL per well).
Place the cell plate in the 37°C incubator on a shake rack at 1,000 RPM.
Use a multichannel pipette to add 50 μL Freestyle F17 medium into each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 5 μL of DNA (100 ng/μL) and 2 μL of PEImax (0.1% w/v, pH 7.0) to each well.
Swirl the mixture immediately to mix.
Incubate the mixture at 20°C–25°C for 10 min.
Add DNA-PEI mixture to cells and gently mix by swirling.
Place cell plates in the 37°C incubator on a shake rack at 1,000 RPM.
Add 0.5 mL of pre-warmed cell culture supplemental medium to each well of cells 24 h post-transfection.
Add 7.5 μL of 500 mM sodium valproate (prepared using deionized water) to each well of cells after 4 days post-transfection (final concentration = 3.75 mM).
Transfer 50 μL of each well of transfected cells into a 96-well plate using a multichannel pipette or VIAFLO 96-channel electronic pipette.
Centrifuge the plate at 3,000 × g for 30 minutes to pellet cells and cellular debris.
Carefully transfer 30 μL of the supernatant (conditioned medium) to a new 96-well plate.
Add 120 μL Octet Sample Diluent to each well using a multichannel pipette or VIAFLO 96-channel electronic pipette.
Use a commercially available antibody to prepare a serial dilution series from 250 to 1.9 mg/L in triplicate for generating a standard curve dataset.
Measure antibody binding curves using an Octet QK instrument and ProA biosensors.
Calculate the antibody concentration estimates based on the generated standard curve.
Use a multichannel pipette to add 100 μL of the 50% bead slurry to each cell culture six days post-transfection.
Return cells to 37°C shake rack in incubator for an overnight (∼16 h) binding step.
Swirl the bead source container frequently while aliquoting beads into cell cultures.
Prepare five plates containing 1 mL 1×DPBS (pH 6.8).
Prepare two plates containing 1 mL deionized water.
Prepare one plate containing 0.4 mL elution buffer (100 mM Sodium acetate, pH 3.6).
Collect ProA magnetic beads from cell culture using Kingfisher Flex 96-well magnetic head and FLEX 96-Tip Comb.
Transfer collected beads to 96-well plates containing 1×DPBS.
Place the plates on the Kingfisher instrument in the order specified: Elution plate, two water plates, three DPBS plates, beads plate (in DPBS), and a final DPBS plate with Tip Comb.
Run Kingfisher purification using the protocol from table:files/protocols_protocol_1682_6.csv.
Immediately after elution, add 8 μL of 3 M Tris-HCl (pH 11) to neutralize the eluted samples.
Transfer the neutralized samples to 96-well 0.22 μm filter plates.
Place the filter plates on top of 96-well collection plates.
Filter by centrifuging at 1,200 × g for 3 minutes.
Store samples in collection plates at 4°C for approximately 4 weeks or at -80°C for long-term storage.
Assess total recombinant expression level by measuring absorbance at 280 nm.
Purify material using Kingfisher ProA purification to recover species containing an Fc region.
Analyze ProA samples with non-reducing Microchip Capillary Electrophoresis (nrMCE).
Conduct Analytical Size-exclusion Chromatography (aSEC) for product quality assessment.
Calculate ProA yield by measuring absorbance at 280 nm.
Transfer 140 μL of each sample into A280-compatible plates using a multichannel pipette or VIAFLO 96 channel electronic pipette.
Measure absorbance at 280 nm with an instrument such as Multiskan Go.
Calculate protein concentration using the Beer-Lambert Law formula: Concentration (mg/mL) = A280 / molar extinction coefficient.
Calculate ProA yield: ProA yield (mg/L) = concentration (mg/mL) × elution volume (mL) / cell culture volume (L).
Use the Caliper LabChip GXII for Non-reducing Microchip Capillary Electrophoresis (nrMCE).
Equilibrate the Protein Express Reagent Kit and one Protein Express Assay LabChip to 20°C–25˚C (∼30 min).
Calculate the amount of nrMCE sample buffer needed to distribute 21 μL to each sample.
Add an additional 20% excess to account for pipetting error.
Transfer the required volume of nrMCE sample buffer stock to a separate container.
Thaw an aliquot(s) of iodoacetamide.
Add the appropriate amount of iodoacetamide to the separate container and gently mix.
Transfer 6 μL samples to 96-well microplates.
Add 21 μL nrMCE sample buffer from the reservoir to each well.
Cover with adhesive foil.
Gently vortex to mix.
Centrifuge at 2,200 × g for 30 seconds.
Heat microplates at 85°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at 2,200 × g for 30 seconds after heating.
Remove foil and add 105 μL water to each sample.
Pipette up and down to mix thoroughly.
Cover with adhesive foil.
Centrifuge at 2,200 × g for 30 seconds.
Visually inspect wells to ensure no air bubbles are present.
Re-centrifuge samples if necessary to remove air bubbles.
Break bubbles using clean pipet tips if needed.
Place the microplate in the instrument platform, aligning with the “A1” marking on the platform edge.
Gently vortex the HT Protein Express Ladder tube after warming to 20°C–25˚C.
Pulse centrifuge the HT Protein Express Ladder tube using a mini centrifuge at approximately 2,000 × g.
Transfer 12 μL to a 0.2 mL microtube.
Add 120 μL water to the microtube.
Pipette up and down to mix thoroughly.
Reverse pipette 520 μL of Protein Express Gel Matrix to the top basket of the provided spin filter.
Centrifuge HT Protein Express Dye Solution briefly at 2,000 × g.
Transfer 20 μL of centrifuged dye solution to the spin filter containing the Gel Matrix.
Cap the filter and invert it.
Vortex until the solution is well mixed.
Centrifuge the capped filter at 9,000 × g for 6 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the filter after centrifugation.
Label the tube after discarding the filter.
Minimize light exposure to the labeled tube.
Reverse pipette 250 μL of Protein Express Gel Matrix to a separate spin filter.
Centrifuge this new filter setup at 9,000 × g for 6 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Discard this filter after centrifugation.
Label and minimize light exposure to the tube.
Remove parafilm covering from the wells of the chip storage box.
Aspirate liquid from active wells using a pipette tip attached to a vacuum line, ensuring not to touch the center region of the well bottom.
Wash each active well with ultrapure water 2–3 times using the vacuum line to aspirate after each wash.
Proceed immediately to the next step without allowing the wells to dry out.
Load the recommended amount of Ladder solution into the corresponding chip wells according to the instrument manual and desired number of runs.
Load the recommended amount of Gel-Dye Solution into the corresponding chip wells according to the instrument manual and desired number of runs.
Load the recommended amount of Destain solution into the corresponding chip wells according to the instrument manual and desired number of runs.
Transfer 750 μL of HT Protein Express Wash Buffer to a provided 0.75 mL Buffer Tube.
Place the prepared chip and Buffer Tube in the instrument platform.
Run the assay using default settings.
Using Caliper LabChip software, quantify the area under the curve for pre-main peak (pre-MP), main peak (MP), and post-main peak (post-MP) as a percent of total area for each sample.
Run several control runs prior to experimental samples.
Use a blank sample to identify any signals originating from buffer or HPLC system.
Run a Gel Filtration Standard prepared according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Analyze a control antibody to ensure column and instruments are functioning properly.
Run Standards and Control Abs at the end of a sample sequence to ensure consistent column performance throughout the sequence.
Install hardware according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Create and save an instrument method using the Instrument Method Wizard.
Specify run time, flow rate, inlets, and a description.
Create and save a processing method using the Processing Method Wizard.
Specify components for annotation (i.e., pre-MP, MP, post-MP).
Select and save a report template layout following on-screen instructions.
Navigate to the instrument control console and manually switch on all required devices before starting a run.
Ensure status of all devices reads as “Ready” before beginning.
Create a workflow sequence using the eWorkflow Wizard containing the desired number of runs.
Enter sample information in the Data tab, including sample ID, injection volume, position, method, processing method, and relevant details.
Note: For a 300 mm Zenix-C column, injected mass should not exceed 32 μg in no more than approximately 50 μL.
Monitor the initial Standard run progress to ensure proper system performance.
Use the Chromeleon analysis tool suite to quantify the area under the curve for pre-MP, MP, and post-MP as a percent of the total area for each sample after the run sequence is complete.
